record.paper_title: Approximating network dynamics: Some open problems
record.original_question: For a Boolean system N with synchronous update map f and an ODE conversion M in the class D2, Theorem 4.3 proves consistency when f is monotone-stepping. Find a necessary and sufficient condition on f under which the conclusion of Theorem 4.3 holds.

evidence.quote: Indeed, we know that some additional assumption on f is needed in the Theorem 4.3, but being monotone- stepping is not a necessary one. Problem 3. Find a necessary and suﬃcient condition onf for which the conclusion of Theorem 4.3 holds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $V=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and consider a Boolean dynamical system $N=(\{0,1\}^n, f)$ with synchronous update map $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$, so that the Boolean trajectory from a state $x_0\in\{0,1\}^n$ is $x_{k+1}=f(x_k)$.

An "ODE conversion" $M$ of $N$ is a continuous-time dynamical system on a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ together with a quantization map $q:\Omega\to\{0,1\}^n$ (componentwise thresholding at $1/2$) such that $M$ is built from $f$ in a prescribed way. We restrict attention to a fixed class $\mathcal{D}_2$ of such ODE conversions; concretely, $\mathcal{D}_2$ consists of systems
$$\dot y_i(t)=F_i(y(t)),\qquad i=1,\dots,n,$$
where each $F_i$ is Lipschitz, the unit cube $[0,1]^n$ is forward invariant, and on each Boolean orthant $B_x=\{y:q(y)=x\}$ the vector field points monotonically toward $f(x)$ (i.e., $\operatorname{sign}(F_i(y))=2f_i(x)-1$ for $y\in B_x$ with $f_i(x)\ne x_i$, and $F_i$ vanishes appropriately when $f_i(x)=x_i$).

Say that $M$ is "consistent" with $N$ if for every initial condition $y_0\in\Omega$ with $q(y_0)=x_0$, the quantized continuous trajectory $\big(q(y(t_k))\big)_{k\ge 0}$ — sampled at the successive times $t_k$ at which $q(y(t))$ changes — coincides with the Boolean trajectory $(x_k)_{k\ge 0}$.

Call $f$ "monotone-stepping" if for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and every coordinate $i$ with $f_i(x)\ne x_i$, the sign of the change in coordinate $i$ is preserved along the Boolean orbit until it agrees with $f$, i.e., once $f$ requests a transition $x_i\to 1-x_i$, no intermediate reversal occurs in coordinate $i$ before that flip is realized.

It is known that if $f$ is monotone-stepping, then every $M\in\mathcal{D}_2$ is consistent with $N$, and that monotone-stepping is sufficient but not necessary.

Problem. Determine a necessary and sufficient condition on the synchronous update map $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$ under which every ODE conversion $M\in\mathcal{D}_2$ of $N$ is consistent with $N$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search found related work on consistency between Boolean networks and Glass-type ODE conversions, distinguishing one-stepping from monotone-stepping conditions, but no source providing a necessary and sufficient criterion characterizing exactly those update maps $f$ for which the consistency conclusion holds. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Two classes of ODE models with switch-like behavior
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses sufficient conditions (one-stepping, monotone-stepping) for consistency between Boolean and ODE (Glass-type) models, without giving a necessary-and-sufficient characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature provides only sufficient conditions for Boolean–ODE consistency.

status_evidence.title: Complementing ODE-Based System Analysis Using Boolean Networks Derived from an Euler-Like Transformation
status_evidence.snippet: Provides Euler-like ODE-to-Boolean transformations under monotonicity-style assumptions but does not characterize necessity.
status_evidence.claim: No necessary-and-sufficient criterion appears in related ODE-Boolean conversion literature.
